newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, HINGIS TO ENTER OPEN FRAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, HINGIS TO ENTER OPEN FRAY.

text.p: Undisputed men's favourite Pete Sampras and the crowd favourite in the women's draw, Swiss starlet Martina Hingis, lead the action on the second day of the Australian Open on Tuesday.

With champion Boris Becker out of the running after his first-round defeat on Monday, world number one Sampras looks to have an almost clear run to his second Australian Open title and Romanian qualifier Dinu Pescariu should not detain him on centre court at Melbourne Park.

The 26-year-old American ended 1996 on a high note by winning the ATP Tour world championship in Hanover and was again in excellent form at the start of this year reaching the final of the Colonial Classic exhibition event on Saturday.
Sampras and his 169th-ranked opponent have never played each other, partly because the Romanian has qualified for only one other grand slam event -- the French Open in 1991.
Hingis, however, may have a tougher assignment against Germany's Barbara Rittner, who last year reached the fourth round of the French Open.
The fourth-seeded Swiss player has soared up the rankings in the last 12 months and is unbeaten in singles matches in two tournaments this year.
Still only 16 years of age, her tennis playing contemporaries believe she is the most likely successor to current number one Steffi Graf.

Hingis has been the form player on the women's tour reaching the final in five of her last six singles tournaments -- winning on three occasions including the Sydney International event last Saturday.
The draw favours a final clash between the Swiss prodigy and Graf.
In one of the most exciting women's matches in 1996, the pair slugged out a five-set final of the year-ending WTA Tour championship with Graf the victor.

Graf has had very little preparation for the Australian Open after falling ill at the end of the year, and on Monday she had hardly warmed-up against Janette Husarova before the Slovakian was forced to retire injured.
Hingis's victim in the Sydney final, Jennifer Capriati, continues her comeback with a match against fellow American Jolene Watanabe.
Second seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain starts her bid for a first Australian Open title with an evening match against Italy's Gloria Pizzichini, ranked 53 in the world.
Sanchez Vicario, 26, has failed to win a grand slam title since 1994 when she won both the French and U.S. Opens.
Big-serving Croat Goran Ivanisevic, the third seed, has been struggling for form but should encounter few difficulties against wildcard Ben Ellwood of Australia when the pair meet on court one.
Double Australian Open champion Jim Courier kicks off his tournament against Sjeng Schalken of the Netherlands.
